questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the following word: PREVALENT
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the following word:

PREVALENT
questions.solution: 'Prevalent' means widespread or commonly occurring. Example: In some countries, malaria is prevalent. 'Rare' means uncommon or not frequently found.  Example: The pink diamond was rare and valuable.

questions.question: What is the style used in writing the given passage?
questions.questionHtml: What is the style used in writing the given passage?
questions.solution: An argumentative style of writing presents a specific viewpoint on a topic and supports it with evidence and logical reasoning. In the given passage, the author presents the viewpoint that the present crisis in the Indian scenario is due to the lack of moral values, character-building incentives, and good cultural values.

questions.question: Select from among the given options the most appropriate title for the passage.
questions.questionHtml: Select from among the given options the most appropriate title for the passage.
questions.solution: The most appropriate title for the given passage is "Lack of Moral Values". This is because the entire passage is focused on discussing how the lack of moral values is responsible for the crisis prevalent in Indian society.

questions.question: Which of the following facts is mentioned in the given passage?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following facts is mentioned in the given passage?

options.text: Lack of effective leadership resulted in the failure of Indian society to provide a new direction to its people.
options.html: Lack of effective leadership resulted in the failure of Indian society to provide a new direction to its people.

options.text: For a successful system of governance, moral values are not essential.
options.html: For a successful system of governance, moral values are not essential.

options.text: Government is responsible for the moral and cultural behaviour of people.
options.html: Government is responsible for the moral and cultural behaviour of people.

options.text: Moral and cultural values account for the crisis in Indian society.
options.html: Moral and cultural values account for the crisis in Indian society.

questions.solution: The passage highlights that even after independence, Indian society could not evolve an effective leadership that could provide a new direction to the people. This lack of effective leadership is one of the reasons for the present crisis in Indian society.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym for the following word: INCENTIVE
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym for the following word:

INCENTIVE
questions.solution: 'Incentive' means a motivating factor or reward. Example: The bonus served as an incentive for hard work. 'Inducement' means a persuasion or incentive. Example: The promise of a promotion was a powerful inducement.

questions.question: What is the tone of the passage?
questions.questionHtml: What is the tone of the passage?
questions.solution: The tone of the passage can be described as "accusive" because it presents an unfolding situation where a harmful drug, Xandersol, has contaminated the local water supply and several parties are being blamed for this incident.

questions.question: Why are the pharmaceutical companies under scrutiny?
questions.questionHtml: Why are the pharmaceutical companies under scrutiny?

options.text: Xandersol was spilled from a pharmaceutical company
options.html: Xandersol was spilled from a pharmaceutical company

questions.solution: The pharmaceutical companies are under scrutiny because the drug Xandersol, which is being blamed for numerous illnesses and deaths, has somehow entered the city water system.

questions.question: What is the theme of the passage?
questions.questionHtml: What is the theme of the passage?

options.text: Plight of the residents in Anchorstown
options.html: Plight of the residents in Anchorstown

questions.solution: The theme of the passage is centered around the Xandersol spill in Anchorstown. The passage highlights the contamination of the city water system with the potentially lethal drug, Xandersol, and its consequences, including numerous illnesses and deaths among Anchorstown residents.

questions.question: Identify the appropriate fact from the passage.
questions.questionHtml: Identify the appropriate fact from the passage.

options.text: Residents have started using makeshift Xandersol filters
options.html: Residents have started using makeshift Xandersol filters

questions.solution: From the passage, it is mentioned that "In desperation, residents have resorted to fitting out their taps with makeshift Xandersol filters." This statement provides the fact that residents, concerned about the contamination of the drinking water with Xandersol, have taken action by installing makeshift filters to safeguard their drinking water.

questions.question: What is the appropriate title for the passage?
questions.questionHtml: What is the appropriate title for the passage?
questions.solution: The appropriate title for the passage is "Adverse effects of Xandersol" because the main focus of the passage is on the harmful consequences of the drug Xandersol. It is being blamed for numerous illnesses and the death of residents in Anchorstown.

questions.question: Which of the following CANNOT be accepted by the general public in India regarding GHI?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following CANNOT be accepted by the general public in India regarding GHI?

options.text: The GHI report takes India’s data from our own National Family Health Survey.
options.html: The GHI report takes India’s data from our own National Family Health Survey.

options.text: One of the two organisations that prepare GHI is from Ireland.
options.html: One of the two organisations that prepare GHI is from Ireland.

options.text: If our children are not tall enough or do not weigh enough, it is an indicator of national hunger.
options.html: If our children are not tall enough or do not weigh enough, it is an indicator of national hunger.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4. 

This is correct because the statement about children's height and weight being indicators of national hunger is a generalization and not specific to the GHI context provided.

questions.question: Select the tone of the last line ‘We are a starving nation!’
questions.questionHtml: Select the tone of the last line ‘We are a starving nation!’
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: option 4.

The phrase "We are a starving nation!" is used ironically to emphasize that the situation described is not literally about starvation, but perhaps a different kind of deprivation.

questions.question: Select the correct summary of the given passage.
questions.questionHtml: Select the correct summary of the given passage.

options.html: The organisations prepared GHI with unquestionable criteria taken all the things into consideration.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2. 

This option accurately captures the essence of the passage by emphasizing the calculation of India's GHI 2022 based on children's height and weight, which is deemed questionable.

questions.question: Which of the following countries is NOT mentioned as better than India in GHI?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following countries is NOT mentioned as better than India in GHI?
questions.solution: The correct answer is: 1) South Arica. South Arica is the only country in the options that is NOT mentioned as better than India in the Global Hunger Index (GHI).

questions.question: In which country is the organisation Welthungerhilfe based?
questions.questionHtml: In which country is the organisation Welthungerhilfe based?
questions.solution: The correct answer is: 1) Germany. The marked option is correct because the passage specifies that the organization Welthungerhilfe is based in Germany.

questions.question: Match the words from the passage with their meanings. 1. moor a. grouped close together 2. gnarled b. open, grassy land 3. clustered c. wrinkled and rough in look
questions.questionHtml:
Match the words from the passage with their meanings.

 1.

moor

 a.

grouped close together

 2.

gnarled

 b.

open, grassy land

 3.

clustered

 c.

wrinkled and rough in look
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1 - b, 2 - c, 3 - a'.

Key Points

  • Let us look at the meaning of the given words - 
    • moor - a tract of open uncultivated upland, typically covered with heather. So, 1 matches with b.
    • gnarled - knobbly, rough, and twisted, especially with age. So, 2 matches with c.
    • clustered - growing or situated in a group. So, 3 matches with a.
  • Thus, the correct order of matching is 1 - b, 2 - c, 3 - a, which is reflected in option 4.

questions.question: The narrator’s opinion about Baskerville was that he: (Select the correct option) a. was a man of strength and pride b. was dangerous looking with an angry face c. would be a difficult person to handle d. would be willing to risk his life in time of danger e. belonged to a noble family
questions.questionHtml:
The narrator’s opinion about Baskerville was that he: (Select the correct option)

a. was a man of strength and pride

b. was dangerous looking with an angry face

c. would be a difficult person to handle

d. would be willing to risk his life in time of danger

e. belonged to a noble family
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'a, d, e'.

Key Points

  • In the first paragraph of the given passage the narrator provides his opinion regarding Baskerville through the following lines - 
  • I felt more than ever how true a descendant he was of that long line of high-blooded, fiery, and masterful men.
    • - High- blooded means someone of noble birth which show statement e to be correct. 
  • There were pride, valour, and strength in his thick brows, his sensitive nostrils, and his large hazel eyes.
    • ​This line proves the validity of statement a.
  • If on that forbidding moor a difficult and dangerous quest should lie before us, this was at least a comrade for whom one might venture to take a risk with the certainty that he would bravely share it.
    • ​This proves the validity of statement d.
  • Thus, off the given statements regarding Baskerville's character, the narrator's opinion matches with a, d, e. 
  • Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The visitors were received ______ at the station.
questions.questionHtml: The visitors were received ______ at the station.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'with respect'. 

Key Points

  • The third line of the second paragraph in the given passage states:
    • Our coming was evidently a great event, for station-master and porters clustered around us to carry out our luggage.
  • The narrator also mentions how a carriage was already waiting for them at the station. 
  • From this, we can conclude, that they were received with respect at the station. 
  • Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Throughout the description of the character and setting, the writer creates a sense of ______.
questions.questionHtml: Throughout the description of the character and setting, the writer creates a sense of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'mystery'.

Key Points

  • The given passage is narrated by someone who is travelling to a place with another person. 
  • In the first paragraph, the narrator provides the reader with a description of his fellow traveler whose name we learn is Baskerville. The narrator also describes the place where they were going by stating that it looked 'like some fantastic landscape in a dream.' The narrator ends this paragraph by stating how he was glad of Baskerville's company in case they faced a forbidding quest at their destination - the moors. 
  •  In the second paragraph also the narrator continues highlighting the mysterious nature
    • ​when he talks about  - 'there stood two soldierly men in dark uniforms who leaned upon their short rifles and glanced keenly at us as we passed.'
    • and when he describes the landscape - 'but behind the peaceful and sunlit countryside there rose ever, dark against the evening sky, the long, gloomy curve of the moor, broken by the jagged and sinister hills.'
  • From the above we can conclude that the narrator was creating a sense of mystery. 
  • Thus, option 1 is the correct answer.

questions.question: What seemed special about the place for Baskerville?
questions.questionHtml: What seemed special about the place for Baskerville?

options.text: He had vague recollections about it.
options.html: He had vague recollections about it.

options.text: It was a place he had dreamt of visiting.
options.html: It was a place he had dreamt of visiting.

options.text: It was a dangerous looking place.
options.html: It was a dangerous looking place.

options.text: His family had held a position of power there.
options.html: His family had held a position of power there.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'His family had held a position of power there.'. 

Key Points

  • The second line of the first paragraph in the given passage states:
    • '... I read upon his eager face how much it meant to him, this first sight of that strange spot where the men of his blood had held sway so long and left their mark so deep.'
  • From this, we can conclude, that Baskerville's ancestors held some sort of power over the place they were visiting. 
  • Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The purpose of the stranger’s visit is:
questions.questionHtml: The purpose of the stranger’s visit is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "to consult him"

Key Points

  • The theme of the passage is an episode from the famous Sherlock Holmes novel where a stranger(Dr. Mortimer) approaches Sherlock with a peculiar case.
  • In the fourth paragraph of the passage, it is stated that the stranger wanted to hire Mr. Holmes to solve a  serious problem he was facing.
  • It is mentioned in the last line of the fourth paragraph. He was meeting with Mr. Holmes as the latter was the second-best expert in this field in Europe.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: Holmes says, “I observe from your forefinger that you make your own cigarettes. Have no hesitation in lighting one.” This remark shows that Holmes:
questions.questionHtml: Holmes says, “I observe from your forefinger that you make your own cigarettes. Have no hesitation in lighting one.” This remark shows that Holmes:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "is a keen observer"

Key Points

  • In the second paragraph of the passage, it is mentioned that Mr. Holmes deduces that Dr.Mortimer(stranger) is a smoker.
  • Mr. Holmes observes this fact by observing the forefinger of Dr. Mortimer closely.
  • He deduces that Dr. Mortmer makes his own cigarettes and invites him to light one.

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: Match the words with the meanings as used in the extract. Word Meaning 1. agile a. with complete accuracy 2. presume b. believe something to be true 3. precisely c. able to move quickly and easily
questions.questionHtml:
Match the words with the meanings as used in the extract.

Word  Meaning
1. agile  a. with complete accuracy
2. presume  b. believe something to be true
3. precisely c. able to move quickly and easily
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "1 - c, 2 - b, 3 - a"

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meaning of the word with reference to the passage.
  • Agile - able to move quickly and easily. The word agile is used in reference to the fingers of Dr. Mortimer. In the third paragraph, it is stated that his fingers moved so quickly and restlessly like the antenna of an insect.
  • Presume - believe something to be true. In the third paragraph, Mr. Holmes believes that Dr. Mortimer is not just here to compliment his skull but there must be another pressing concern.
  • Precisely -  with complete accuracy. In the second last sentence of the paragraph, Dr. Mortimer states that the work of Monsieur Bertillon who was the first choice of an expert appeals to the man of the precisely scientific mind. The word precisely is used in the context of men who work with natural sciences who believe in being accurate to the last degree.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.question: What is the strange visitor most interested in, according to Sherlock Holmes?
questions.questionHtml: What is the strange visitor most interested in, according to Sherlock Holmes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Sherlock's skull"

Key Points

  • In the first paragraph of the passage, the stranger(Dr. Mortimer) mentions that he envies Sherlock's skull.
  • He further elaborates on this fascination by stating "I had hardly expected so long a skull or such well-marked frontal head. A cast of your skull, sir, until the original is available, would be an ornament to any anthropological museum."
  • The strange visitor also states" It is not my intention to be fulsome, but I confess that I covet your skull,”.

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: The visitor has chosen Holmes to solve his problem because he believes that:
questions.questionHtml: The visitor has chosen Holmes to solve his problem because he believes that:

options.text: Holmes is inferior to Monsieur Bertillon who has a scientific mind
options.html: Holmes is inferior to Monsieur Bertillon who has a scientific mind

options.text: a study of his skull would be of great value to him
options.html: a study of his skull would be of great value to him

options.text: Holmes is an unpractical man more interested in people’s habits
options.html: Holmes is an unpractical man more interested in people’s habits

options.text: Holmes is most suited in helping solve an extraordinary practical matter
options.html: Holmes is most suited in helping solve an extraordinary practical matter

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Holmes is most suited in helping solve an extraordinary practical matter"

Key Points

  • In the second last sentence of the passage, Dr. Mortimer(visitor) mentions that he has chosen Mr. Holmes owing to his pragmatic approach.
  • Let's refer to the line -
    • "'But as a practical man of affairs, it is acknowledged that you stand alone." ( From ''I said, sir.......not inadvertently'')
  • From the above-mentioned line, it is clear that the visitor chose Holmes to solve his problem because he believes that Holmes is most suited in helping solve an extraordinary practical matter.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.question: The author points out that in the 19th century, swill milk was linked with thousands of infant deaths. Which ONE of the actions below would have, if familiar, available and practicable for the people of that time, saved these children?
questions.questionHtml: The author points out that in the 19th century, swill milk was linked with thousands of infant deaths. Which ONE of the actions below would have, if familiar, available and practicable for the people of that time, saved these children?

options.text: Feeding the cows uncontaminated healthy food
options.html: Feeding the cows uncontaminated healthy food

options.text: Freezing the milk to remove the pollutants
options.html: Freezing the milk to remove the pollutants

questions.solution:
Thorough reading can give you the answer to this question easily.

In the last few lines of the passage, it is mentioned that cows were fed the filthy runoff from inner-city breweries which turned their milk blue, and this was linked with thousands of infant deaths. Thus the correct reason is given in option 3.

Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.question: 'Lactose intolerance' is ________.
questions.questionHtml: 'Lactose intolerance' is ________.

options.text: linked to discovery and propagation of plant milk
options.html: linked to discovery and propagation of plant milk

options.text: experience and suffering problems in the digestive system
options.html: experience and suffering problems in the digestive system

options.text: a human body not being able to accept cow's milk allergy
options.html: a human body not being able to accept cow's milk allergy

options.text: absence of the enzyme lactase in the gut, creating intolerance for milk
options.html: absence of the enzyme lactase in the gut, creating intolerance for milk

questions.solution:
The answer to this can be found out in the first paragraph and last lines of the second paragraph.

" But for the majority of humans, production of the enzyme lactase plummets after weaning"

"... and then as you get past infancy, to stop producing lactase and become lactose intolerant"

These sentences from the passage tell you that lactose intolerance is the absence of the enzyme lactase in the gut and hence option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: Most adults in India continue to have milk without suffering any of the issues outlined in the passage because ________.
questions.questionHtml: Most adults in India continue to have milk without suffering any of the issues outlined in the passage because ________.

options.html: they have no other source of nutrients to nourish them

"Then you've got a small group of humans that have a mutation which means they maintain production of lactase into adulthood."

It is given here that people in India continue to have milk without suffering any issues because they maintain production of lactase into adulthood.

Thus option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: "More than 90% of adults in countries such as the UK, Sweden and Ireland can drink milk without suffering any ill effects" because _________.
questions.questionHtml: "More than 90% of adults in countries such as the UK, Sweden and Ireland can drink milk without suffering any ill effects" because _________.

questions.question: What is this passage about?
questions.questionHtml: What is this passage about?

options.text: Weaning and the plummeting enzyme lactase

These things mentioned in the passage tells us that the passage is mainly about milk and lactose intolerance.

Option 3 is the right answer.

questions.question: Which line in the passage most strongly indicates that beavers simply love being in or near water?
questions.questionHtml: Which line in the passage most strongly indicates that beavers simply love being in or near water?

options.text: The dam was so firm and broad that it was easy to walk along.
options.html: The dam was so firm and broad that it was easy to walk along.

options.text: The only access to the dwelling is under the water.
options.html: The only access to the dwelling is under the water.

options.text: The beaver had made a dam out of the quickly flowing stream.
options.html: The beaver had made a dam out of the quickly flowing stream.

options.text: The water is the beaver's element.
options.html: The water is the beaver's element.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4, i.e. 'The water is the beaver's element.'

In the given passage, it is clearly mentioned that "The water is the beaver's element." in the third paragraph, which means that the beaver's simply love being in or near water.

Hence, the line provided in option 4 most strongly indicates that weavers simply love being in or near water.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

options.text: The beaver has to make its dwelling frostproof before it starts snowing.
options.html: The beaver has to make its dwelling frostproof before it starts snowing.

options.text: The beaver can move quickly and easily on land and in water.
options.html: The beaver can move quickly and easily on land and in water.

options.text: Wide stretches of meadows may come into existence on the banks of streams.
options.html: Wide stretches of meadows may come into existence on the banks of streams.

options.text: The access to the beaver's dwelling is under the water.
options.html: The access to the beaver's dwelling is under the water.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2), i.e. 'The beaver can move quickly and easily on land and in water.'

  • Option 1, i.e. "The beaver has to make its dwelling frostproof before it starts snowing." is true. According to the passage, "In the late autumn, before land and water are covered with snow and ice, the beaver has to make its dwelling frostproof."
  • Option 2, i.e. "The beaver can move quickly and easily on land and in water." is not true as they are slow and awkward in land. According to the passage,"The water is the beaver's element. On land, it moves slowly and awkwardly."
  • Option 3, i.e. "Wide stretches of meadows may come into existence on the banks of streams." is true. According to the passage, "Wide stretches of meadow had come into existence on the banks, with flat landing places to which the well-beaten beaver tracks led."
  • Option 4, i.e. "The access to the beaver's dwelling is under the water." is true. According to the passage,"The only access to the dwelling is under the water, and even the forest wolves are not able to pull the firm building apart."

 

Hence, the information provided in option 2 is not true.

questions.question: What evidence in the passage suggests that beavers build strong dwellings?
questions.questionHtml: What evidence in the passage suggests that beavers build strong dwellings?

options.text: The interior is lined with finest wood shavings.
options.html: The interior is lined with finest wood shavings.

options.text: It takes many years of hard work to build the dwelling.
options.html: It takes many years of hard work to build the dwelling.

options.text: Even the forest wolves cannot pull the dwelling apart.
options.html: Even the forest wolves cannot pull the dwelling apart.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4), i.e. 'Even the forest wolves cannot pull the dwelling apart.'

In the passage, it is mentioned that the forest wolves cannot break the dwellings of the beavers. It can be said that the dwellings of the beavers are strongly built because it is so strong that no wild animal can pull it apart.

Therefore, the information provided in option 4 is the evidence which suggests that beavers build strong dwellings.

questions.question: How does a beaver ensure that its castle is well ventilated?
questions.questionHtml: How does a beaver ensure that its castle is well ventilated?

options.text: The timber is piled upto ten feet high on the castle.
options.html: The timber is piled upto ten feet high on the castle.

options.text: The long stems are gnawed into small sections.
options.html: The long stems are gnawed into small sections.

options.text: The upper logs are loosely placed.
options.html: The upper logs are loosely placed.

options.text: The logs are covered with earth and plants.
options.html: The logs are covered with earth and plants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e. 'The upper logs are loosely placed'.

According to the given passage, "The upper logs were put loosely together so that the air could pass through to the interior."

The beavers used to place the upper logs loosely in order to keep the castle well ventilated.

Hence, option 3 is the best fit.

questions.question: The beavers can change the landscape by:
questions.questionHtml: The beavers can change the landscape by:

options.text: building castles with great heaps of logs.
options.html: building castles with great heaps of logs.

options.text: dragging the logs of wood to the dwelling.
options.html: dragging the logs of wood to the dwelling.

options.text: building dams that can convert a wooded alley into a lake.
options.html: building dams that can convert a wooded alley into a lake.

options.text: swimming in the water along with ducks and trouts.
options.html: swimming in the water along with ducks and trouts.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e. 'building dams that can convert a wooded alley into a lake.'

According to the passage, "The beaver's activities can change whole landscapes. With this dam, for instance, on which I was standing, beavers had turned a whole wooded alley into a lake."

In this passage, it is said that with the activities of the beavers, the whole landscape can be changed and one of those activities was building the dams.

Therefore option 3 is the answer.

questions.question: Which of the following techniques has been used by the author of the passage to convey the message?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following techniques has been used by the author of the passage to convey the message?
questions.solution: The technique used by the author of the passage to convey the message is "Humour and exaggeration." The author employs a humorous tone to address the seriousness of the issue and uses exaggeration to make a point about the widespread nature of stupidity in society, politics, and social media.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the solution to the issue of stupidity in society?
questions.questionHtml: According to the passage, what is the solution to the issue of stupidity in society?

options.text: Teaching students how to pass tests
options.html: Teaching students how to pass tests

options.text: Encouraging critical thinking and problem-solving skills
options.html: Encouraging critical thinking and problem-solving skills

questions.solution: According to the passage, the solution to the issue of stupidity in society is "Encouraging critical thinking and problem-solving skills." The author emphasizes the need to value intelligence, demand well-informed leaders, and teach children to think critically, rather than just memorizing information.

questions.question: What is the tone of the passage?
questions.questionHtml: What is the tone of the passage?
questions.solution: The tone of the passage is "Sarcastic." The author uses a sarcastic tone to criticize the prevalence of stupidity in society, politics, and the education system, while also humorously calling for a return to valuing intelligence and critical thinking.

questions.question: According to the author of the passage, who among the following is NOT responsible for the spread of stupidity?
questions.questionHtml: According to the author of the passage, who among the following is NOT responsible for the spread of stupidity?
questions.solution: According to the passage, the authors do not blame 'children' for the spread of stupidity. Instead, politicians, the education system, and individuals are held accountable for contributing to the epidemic of stupidity, highlighting the failure in leadership, educational approaches, and personal discernment, respectively. Therefore, the correct answer is 'Children'.

questions.question: What could be a suitable title for the passage?

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word with reference to its usage in the passage. Debilitating
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word with reference to its usage in the passage.

Debilitating
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Invigorating

Key Points

  • The word "debilitating" in the passage is used to describe certain weaknesses of traditional Indian firms, suggesting that these weaknesses are debilitating, meaning they make the firms less effective or hinder their performance. (कम प्रभावी या उनके प्रदर्शन में बाधा)
  • In the context of the passage, the most appropriate antonym for "debilitating" would be "invigorating."
  • "Invigorating" means to give strength, energy, or vitality. (ऊर्जा या जीवन शक्ति देने के लिए)
  • So, in the opposite sense, weaknesses that are invigorating would enhance or strengthen the performance of the firms, which contrasts with the negative impact implied by the term "debilitating" in the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Additional Information

  • Enfeebling: Weakening or making someone or something feeble, physically or mentally. (किसी व्यक्ति या वस्तु को शारीरिक या मानसिक रूप से कमजोर करना)
  • Crippling: Causing severe damage or impairment, often rendering something or someone unable to function effectively. (गंभीर क्षति या क्षति पहुंचाना, अक्सर किसी चीज़ या व्यक्ति को प्रभावी ढंग से कार्य करने में असमर्थ बना देना)
  • Undermining: Gradually weakening or eroding the foundation, support, or strength of someone or something, often through subtle or indirect means. (किसी व्यक्ति या वस्तु की नींव, समर्थन या ताकत को धीरे-धीरे कमजोर करना या नष्ट करना)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word with reference to its usage in the passage. Asphyxiating
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word with reference to its usage in the passage.

Asphyxiating
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Smothering

Key Points

  • "Asphyxiating" refers to the action of causing someone or something to suffocate or deprive them of air. (किसी व्यक्ति या वस्तु का दम घोंटने या उन्हें हवा से वंचित करने की क्रिया)
  • In the context of the passage, it is used metaphorically to describe the oppressive or stifling nature of the hierarchy.
  • Similarly, "smothering" also conveys the idea of suppressing or stifling. (दबाने का विचार)
  • So, it is the appropriate synonym for "asphyxiating" in the given context.
  • Both terms suggest a sense of constriction and inhibition, emphasizing the negative impact of an overwhelming hierarchy.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Additional Information

  • Emancipating: Freeing or releasing someone or something from constraints, restrictions, or oppressive conditions, often related to social or legal constraints. (किसी व्यक्ति या वस्तु को बाधाओं, प्रतिबंधों या दमनकारी स्थितियों से मुक्त करना या रिहा करना, जो अक्सर सामाजिक या कानूनी बाधाओं से संबंधित होती हैं)
  • Liberating: Granting freedom or independence, allowing someone or something to break free from constraints or restrictions. (स्वतंत्रता प्रदान करना, किसी व्यक्ति या चीज़ को बाधाओं या प्रतिबंधों से मुक्त होने की अनुमति देना)
  • Unfettering: Removing or loosening fetters or constraints, freeing from restrictions or limitations. (बाधाओं को हटाना या ढीला करना, प्रतिबंधों या सीमाओं से मुक्त होना)
